title: Enhancing income & food security in the Occupied Palestine Territory
description: This is the Gaza component  of the ECHO proposal. It has CFW and FS activities.   The proposed intervention will implement cash for work (CFW) and Food Security activities (rabbits' breeding and backyard garden production). The CFW will provide a much needed cash injection for 3,031 beneficiaries (433 households) to improve their food consumption, cover other basic needs and to reduce their debts. Through the CFW activities 47Km of Agricultural Roads will be rehabilitated and 25 Schools will be developed.   The FS activities aim to provide longer -term improvement in diet and a raise of income for 3,150 beneficiaries (450 needy households).

The study will pay particular attention to specific opportunities that might produce significant benefits for women and the poorer smallholder farmers supplying these businesses

title: Improving trans-boundary agribusiness responsible land governance in C,L,M,V II
description: Oxfam in Myanmar seeks to contribute to the overall Mekong Regional Land Governance (MRLG) outcomes by engaging Myanmar and international agribusiness companies on land issues. In Myanmar, Oxfam will engage with local companies in Oxfam -organised workshops and meetings to raise awareness of land issues in the Shan and Kachin States. In addition, Oxfam will conduct research on company -community conflicts surrounding land acquisition in Myanmar, and support Oxfam in Vietnam's scoping trip and roundtable with Vietnamese companies in Myanmar. Oxfam in Myanmar will also participate in regional MRLG exchange trips and forums.

title: Covid-19 Response in Mali
description: The project aims to support the response plan of Oxfam's covid -19 in Mali and particularly in the cIrcle of Bourem, Gao Region in the fight against the covid -19 pandemic through exchanges with communities to better adapt the prevention measures of Covid -19 to their context.  The intended result is to promote good hygienic practices and physical distance measures that can strengthen the fight against the spread of COVID -19  through:   -  Mass communication  in local radio stations where the project will aim to reach 100,000 people living in the communes of Bourem, Taboye, Temera and Bamba in the Bourem district. The choice of the circle in collaboration with the community radio stations in the area concerned for the broadcasting of the messages with the project implementing partner.  - The project team will engage in dialogue with community leaders and elected municipal officials, including the various groups and community mobilizers, to ensure their support and facilitate a change of behaviour in the face of the Covid -19 pandemic.   - In addition, posters will be produced to reach as many vulnerable people as possible, including the disabled, marginalized, etc. The project team will also produce posters for the public to use in the community. title: Community-Based Integrated Health Care Project, Yemen
description: This three years project aims at improving the health status of poor women, men and children in 22 remote communities in Hadhramout through establishing community health financing schemes, strengthening the capacities of the district health systems, training of women as health providers and community health promotion. It is building on Oxfam's experience in the Wadi and Desert Region of Hadhramout, and piloting in the coastal areas. Oxfam implement this project through its staff in the sub  -office in Hadhramout in partnership with the Regional Health Offices, and in collaboration with other key stakeholders.

description: The INGO Forum aims to influence and increase the effectiveness and coherence of humanitarian relief and development aid in Myanmar. Specific areas of activity will cover 1) supporting coordination amongst members and with external stakeholders; 2) sharing information and providing member services, including advice on navigating the operational space; 3) producing common position and influencing key stakeholders on humanitarian and development issues. In doing so, it supports an enabling environment for INGOs to better fulfil their mandates and serve people in need in Myanmar.

title: Lifesaving Response to Returnees and Refugees from Sudan, South Sudan
description: The project will provide rapid emergency Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) response to at least 10,000 refugees and returnees in Renk (7,000) and Melut (3,000) Transit Centres. Emergency WASH infrastructure and services will be developed/installed  to meet critical WASH needs and work towards sustainable solutions by linking humanitarian interventions to long -term measures. The interventions will include emergency water trucking, pipeline extension from the existing distribution networks (Melut), construction of communal water points/tap stands, water treatment, and water quality monitoring. Oxfam will work closely with the county governments and water utility companies (for both Melut and Renk) in water service provision.

title: Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Response In Saada
description: The protracted crisis in Yemen was exacerbated by the latest interference of external factors, i.e. Saudi -led coalition airstrikes and the siege stopping imports of food, fuel and medical supplies, and has made the situation on the ground much worse. So, the  main objectives of this intervention  is to contribute to diminishing risks related to shortage of water, sanitation ,hygiene and livelihood  for the affected communities in Sa'ada province, through a set of activities which include emergency water trucking, rehabilitation/construction of water and sanitation facilities and dissemination of hygiene messages  .

title: Strengthened Protection and Resilience of Crisis-affected in Lebanon
description: Oxfam's interventions in Lebanon focus on basic service provision that grants refugees life -sustaining access to clean water and sanitation on the one hand, and empowering their communities to identify, process, and address daily protection concerns on the other, all the while highlighting those concerns and gaps in assistance and rights provision to local authorities and key international stakeholders through its advocacy efforts. In the coming years, this approach would prove even more relevant, as refugees are increasingly compelled to make radical decisions about their future  - like returning to Syria or moving to ostensibly more welcoming areas in Lebanon – with often little reliable information to guide those choices. Oxfam's interventions thus focus on equipping refugees with key information pertaining to their access to essential services, civil status documentation, and rights and protective laws against exploitation and coercion. Information shared with target population will increase the knowledge on own rights, existing legal requirements and ways to access relevant services and assistance available in a safe manner, increasing capacity to prevent and mitigate protection risks. With this knowledge, individuals are also expected to be able to contact service providers directly, through the support of a focal point, or by contacting Oxfam staff and partners. Refugee women, often more vulnerable to abuse and harassment, face unique threats that Oxfam, through its partnership with specialized local SGBV case management organizations, addresses systematically within its broader response to the needs of the community. Oxfam's protection monitoring findings, as well as feedback communicated to its staff in the field, highlight fears of forced return and eviction as being the most preoccupying for refugees. title: Empowering communities to respond to conflict-induced protection risks.
description: Oxfam will support existing community structures, or establish a community -based social committee, composed of members from Internally Displaced Person (IDP) and host communities, where these committees should represent most vulnerable people & groups such as (minority groups, internally displaced persons, women, marginalized groups and people with disabilities). In addition, 600 of the most vulnerable people/House -Holds (HHs) and groups who will be targeted in Sadah  include the following: Women headed household, people living with disabilities, single heads of household, child -headed household and marginalized groups ‘'Muhamasheen'', old people, IDPs and persons with chronic illness including mental health disorders: those groups are severely impacted by the ongoing conflict and they are at disproportionate risk during pandemics, as they suffer from hindered access to services and accurate information, often aggravated by stigmatization and arbitrary targeting as shown in needs assessment, and the findings of secondary sources and the primary sources.  Emergency Food Security and Vulnerable Livelihood (EFSVL): Oxfam will target 780 most vulnerable households in Majz district which are at high protection risk to reduce their vulnerability and increase their protection capacities by providing them with sustainable and safer livelihoods and income opportunities. The priority targets include Persons With Disabilities (PWD), minority groups ‘'Muhamasheen'', persons with specific needs, female -headed households, vulnerable children exposed to neglect, abuse, violence and exploitation, or women and girls at risk, including child marriage

title: Emergency WASH and Protection response for IDPs and refugees from Syria
description: With GAC funding: Within the framework of the Regional Refugee and Resilience Plan 2015 (3RP), Oxfam intend to offer a comprehensive and sustainable WASH response, which includes the involvement of local municipalities in Bekaa. Besides 68 Informal settlements (IS) located in six municipalities of North Bekaa, one of the biggest IS of Lebanon (470 households), located in Bar Elias, West Bekaa, will be targeted with a comprehensive WASH intervention and a tailored solid waste management approach. In Bar Elias IS (West Bekaa), drinking water for 470 households will be provided in collaboration with the Bekaa Water Establishment. Water for domestic use will be provided using the recently built wells and pumping facilities and safe chlorination will be ensured. With ECHO Funding: This is an integrated WASH and Protection action aims at contributing to mitigating the protection risks of human -generated violence, coercion, deprivation and abuse, and to reduce public health risks for 7,080 vulnerable people affected by the Syria crisis. Specifically, the Action intends to enable vulnerable individuals and communities to reduce protection risks and safely meet basic WASH needs. Oxfam with partners (AJEM, RDFL, Najdeh) propose a combination of activities aimed at reducing the vulnerability of the population in North Bekaa and Palestinian camps in the North, to protection threats and increasing their capacity by strengthening their knowledge of legal frameworks, services available and of soft -skills to address community problems. This is combined with the establishment of solid linkages with existing services, or the provision of other specialised services that can offer redress to individuals who are victims of negative coping strategies or threats resulting from lack of legal residency and of income. title: Humanitarian Capacity Development and Response Project
description: Yemen is facing a chronic humanitarian crisis. This is exacerbated by recurring conflict and displacement, water scarcity, soaring food prices and high rates of malnutrition and disease. Given the political and economic instability in country, humanitarian assistance is going to be required in Yemen for the foreseeable future. The scale of need exceeds the capacity of the government, and to some extent the humanitarian community, to respond. This project is therefore being developed to provide further support and development to in country structures for effective humanitarian preparedness and response.

description: Oxfam Yemen will implement an integrated program in Hajjah combining targeted food security and livelihood (FSL), water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), disaster risk reduction (DRR) and advocacy to build more resilient communities. FSL will include cash transfers (unconditional cash transfer (UCT) and cash for work (CfW) & other livelihoods activities.  DRR and integrated water resource management (IWRM) will strengthen the communities' resilience to shocks and management of natural resources. On the national level, Oxfam will advocate for gender equality, social protection, and water related issues.

title: Humanitarian Response to the Food Crisis in Kayes, Mali
description: This project is set to launch the Oxfam International (OI) response to the food crisis in Kayes. It aims to help mitigate the risks and shocks of the food insecurity in the most vulnerable communities in Kayes region. The response focuses on 3 phases:  - One aiming at strengthening resilience and avoiding the depletion of the livelihoods assets of the very poor and poor families;   - one during the lean period  aiming at increasing the access to food and the fight against malnutrition;  - and an early recovery of the most vulnerable families.  Advocacy, coordination and monitoring complete these actions.

description: The project would create an enabling environment for dialogue, discussion pertinent issues between Civil Society Organisations (CSOs), communities on one hand and authorities on the other hand. Through this project CSOs capacity will be enhanced to influence policies and monitor service delivery.
